losscase.name: k10k_tree_15_k3_s1_exp_krepp_estimated
losscase.conclusion: the printed loss is attained at a neighbouring support

protocol.question: On real estimated distances, how does the mixture DecoDiPhy actually returns fit the data, measured in the same units as the exact single-source tolerance Theta_1?

measurements.r_dd: R_dd = max_r |y + sum_i p_i dist_T(r, q_i) - d_r| over the observed reference leaves, with the configuration exactly as the tool returned it (bank edge index, p, x from the frozen stage-289 bridge; y = the scalar pendant, which DecoDiPhy splits across placements only for its jplace output and whose parts sum back to it by construction - decodiphy/tree_utils.compute_individual_ys).  Exact rational.
measurements.theta1: imported from stage 298; never recomputed differently
measurements.truth_linf: imported from stage 298 (residual_max) and independently recomputed here as a verification
measurements.ssr: sum_r (pred_r - d_r)^2, float64 - DecoDiPhy's own objective (decodiphy/optimize.py: np.sum((d - (DA @ p + CAl @ x + y)) ** 2))
measurements.lambda1: exhaustive minimum of SSR over every original edge, x in [0,1], y >= 0, p = 1: the L2 analogue of Theta_1, i.e. the best single source in the norm the tool optimises

protocol.norm_caveat: DecoDiPhy minimises SSR, not the L-infinity residual.  Both norms are therefore reported for every configuration, and the single-source baseline is reported in both (Theta_1 and Lambda_1).

run_plan.harvested: every full-panel DecoDiPhy run recorded by stages 289, 293, 294 and 297 on the krepp ANI family, with provenance (file, line, arm, repetition or seed); nothing re-run

new.krepp_placement: 60 cases x {dd_default, dd_true_k}, wall 1800 s, RLIMIT_AS 8 GB, 20 workers
new.travelers: 29 samples x {dd_default}, wall 14400 s, RLIMIT_AS 60 GB, workers sized from the pilot's peak RSS

run_plan.retention: every run retained, including timeouts, memory kills and crashes

verification_plan.route_a: exact rational equality of the min form and the interpolation form on every evaluated run
verification_plan.route_b: whole-case recomputation with scipy.sparse.csgraph.dijkstra on the edge list with the source points inserted as vertices
verification_plan.route_c: prediction rebuilt from DecoDiPhy's own D, C, l matrices on the tree file the bridge writes
verification_plan.route_d: recomputed SSR of the returned configuration against the loss the tool itself reported, for every run
verification_plan.route_e: Lambda_1 against the tool's own k = 1 ladder loss, which it computes by hill climbing over the same edge set
